profile.reading:
This OpenStreetMap record in Yellowstone County, Montana, near Billings, the state's largest city, is tagged as a telecom data center under the name Parsec Data Management. Billings supports a modest local market for IT services, records storage, and managed hosting serving regional businesses, government offices, and the area's energy and agricultural sectors, so a small data management or backup services company operating there would not be surprising on its face.

However, extensive searching turned up no company website, business registration, news coverage, or directory listing under the name Parsec Data Management in Montana. The coordinates recorded for this entry resolve to a residential street in Billings rather than a commercial or industrial address, which is not typical of a purpose built data center. Parsec is also the name of an unrelated and much larger consumer remote desktop and game streaming company, which crowds out search results and makes it harder to confirm whether a distinct Montana business by this name still exists or ever operated at meaningful scale.

Given the absence of any independently verifiable business behind this name, this entry is published without data center specifications. It may reflect a very small local operation, a defunct business, or a mapping error, and none of those possibilities can be distinguished from the available public record.

reading.body:
Parsec Data Management cannot be counted as AI compute capacity, because no verifiable business, address, or specification exists behind the name.

The record is an OpenStreetMap tag in Yellowstone County, Montana, near Billings, labeled as a telecom data center. Its coordinates resolve to a residential street rather than a commercial or industrial site. Searches for the exact business name returned no website, registration, news coverage, or directory listing, only results for the unrelated Parsec remote desktop and game streaming company. The entry carries no megawatt figure, no operator, and no published specifications.

For AI infrastructure, the megawatt figure is the fact that matters, because compute scales with power drawn and power is delivered to buildings. A facility with no stated capacity and no confirmed operator contributes nothing to that accounting. Montana has two mapped data center facilities and zero published megawatt figures from operator spec pages, so the state's position in any compute inventory rests on unquantified entries like this one.

What the data does not establish is whether Parsec Data Management is a very small local operation, a defunct business, or a mapping error. The public record does not distinguish among those. The absence of evidence here is not evidence that no small hosting or records storage business operates in Billings, a city with regional demand from government, energy, and agriculture. It means only that this particular record cannot be verified, and should be excluded from capacity analysis until it can be.
